title: Biomedical AI Quality and Safety Simulator
audience: Clinical learners exploring AI quality, safety, drift, calibration, and transparency
objectives: Recognize covariate shift in a simulated sepsis prediction model.
Compare doing nothing versus retraining under clinical distribution shift.
Evaluate vendor model discrimination and calibration on a mismatched local population.
Build a model card documenting intended clinical use, limitations, metrics, and ethical considerations.

sections.name: Sepsis Drift
sections.purpose: Show how changing patient populations or lab distributions can affect alerts.
sections.how_to_use: Move the months slider, compare lactate distributions, choose a mitigation strategy, and watch false positive rate.

sections.name: Vendor Calibration
sections.purpose: Evaluate whether a vendor model is reliable on the local population.
sections.how_to_use: Adjust population mismatch, review AUC, and inspect calibration to see whether predicted risks match actual risks.

sections.name: Model Card Builder
sections.purpose: Practice clinical model documentation before deployment.
sections.how_to_use: Fill in intended users, caveats, and ethical considerations, then review the generated model card.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the three tabs: drift, vendor calibration, and model card.
For clinical users, emphasize alert fatigue, local validation, calibration, patient population mismatch, and deployment limits.
Explain that high AUC does not guarantee reliable patient-level probabilities.
